sentences.text: Sphenacanthus possessed seven fins, heterodont dentition — teeth of different shapes — and relatively long, deep mandibles.
Fossil evidence suggests this animal was a relatively large shark, likely exceeding one meter in length when fully grown.
Unlike modern sharks, Sphenacanthus inhabited fresh water lagoons and likely hunted small fish.
It is possible that Sphenacanthus preyed on its smaller relatives.
Sphenacanthus was discovered in Carboniferous terrains in Scotland and the Paraná Basin in Brazil, inhabiting ancient fresh water systems.
Findings from the Puertollano Basin in Spain suggest that Sphenacanthus also lived in zones of marine influence, such as brackish waters.
There are 11 recorded fossil occurrences of the genus Sphenacanthus in the Paleobiology Database.
The genus Sphenacanthus was described by Agassiz in 1837.
The type species of the genus Sphenacanthus is Sphenacanthus serrulatus — the specific specimen the genus is based on.
Sphenacanthus belongs to the family Sphenacanthidae.
Sphenacanthus is classified within the order Ctenacanthiformes.
Sphenacanthus is a member of the class Chondrichthyes.
Sphenacanthus belongs to the subclass Elasmobranchii.
Sphenacanthus is an animal within the kingdom Animalia.
Sphenacanthus belongs to the phylum Chordata.
Sphenacanthus lived approximately 359 million years ago and is considered one of the earliest members of the elasmobranch lineage leading to modern sharks.
